title: Python SDK: incremental-response-iterator and event-middleware pattern
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: current Python streaming chat surface exposes low-level event callbacks and forces application developers to either write fragile FSMs or copy helper utilities. Common pain points: 1) combining partial deltas + structured events into a single consumable stream, 2) clean cancellation and backpressure from sync and async paths, 3) retrying or resuming a partially-received stream after transient errors, and 4) adding orthogonal cross-cutting behaviors (logging, metrics, profanity filter, structured transform) without duplicating parsing logic.

Goal: introduce an ergonomic incremental-response iterator API plus a small event-middleware pattern so apps get a single consistent, composable streaming primitive. This should support both sync generators and async async-generators, surface typed events (delta, role, function_call, error, done), and make retries/resume explicit and discoverable. Keep the low-level event callback API for advanced users but make the new surface the recommended path in examples and docs.
technical_notes: API proposal (high level): Client.chat.stream_messages(...) -> AsyncIterator[StreamEvent] and Client.chat.stream_messages_sync(...) -> Iterator[StreamEvent]

StreamEvent is a small tagged union with fields: type in {delta, role, function_call, structured, error, done}, text (optional), token_index (optional, monotonic), metadata (dict for op IDs). We will keep the internal shape stable but expose as Python dataclass-like objects with .type and .text properties.

Middleware: accept a list of callables middleware(event, next) -> next(modified_event). Middleware can be pure (filter/transform) or side-effecting (metrics, logging). Provide three built-in middleware: dedupe-token, structured-collector, and graceful-cancel.

Backpressure: for sync generator we implement an internal bounded queue (configurable via stream_buffer_size) and block producer when full. For async generator we use asyncio.Queue with backpressure; default buffer size 64. Document tradeoffs for latency vs throughput.

Retries & resume: servers will support resume tokens (offsets) in a subset of models. When available, Client will expose resume_token on StreamEvent.done and StreamEvent.error; retry helpers will retry with ?resume_token=. For non-resumable models we add a best-effort idempotent-retry that replays prompts and de-duplicates final chunks by checksum; document cases where this causes duplicated content.

Errors: define StreamInterruptedError (has partial_text and resume_token optional) and StreamMalformedEventError for protocol deviations. Streaming helpers should surface partial_text to callers for graceful degradation and monitoring.

Testing: end-to-end tests against the mock streaming server will assert ordering, cancellation, middleware ordering, and resume behavior. Add property tests to fuzz event interleaving (role/token/structured events).
Migration: keep legacy event callback API: client.chat.on_stream_event(callback) but mark it as advanced. New examples will be the canonical approach in README and quickstarts.
proposed_api_examples:
# middleware example registration:
client.chat.register_stream_middleware([
    sdk.middleware.dedupe_tokens(),
    sdk.middleware.metrics_timer(),
    sdk.middleware.filter_bad_words(blocklist=[...])
])
acceptance_criteria: New async iterator API landing in sdk-python v1.6.0 with documented examples in README
Sync generator equivalent available and tested in integration tests
Built-in middleware primitives (dedupe, structured collector, metrics) implemented and covered by unit tests
Retry & resume semantics documented and an example end-to-end test that resumes using resume_token
Performance: default stream buffering introduces <10ms median overhead on p99 latency for single-stream tests compared to current callback-based impl
Migration doc and two sample apps updated to use new API; deprecation plan for low-level callback surface established
